analysis:
The only change in this PR is one documentation row in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1960). The row is added to the table of daemon-forwarded environment variables, in the section after the LaunchAgent passthrough text. It documents DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS, read in SSDPrefixCachePolicy.incrementalCheckpoints. Values 0/false/no/off write complete checkpoints instead of deltas. No code, config default, or control changes in the supplied evidence, so no executable behavior regressed.

The threat model context is T-041, the encrypted SSD prefix cache. The documentation implies a new incremental or delta checkpoint write mode in the SSD tier (SSDBlockStore, SSDPrefixCache). Per T-041's detection_hint, changes to DBK3 metadata or AAD construction, HMAC lookup-tag derivation, or the TTL and disk budget need fresh review. Those source files are not supplied. The delta format could in principle add on-disk metadata or alter the AAD, lookup-tag or salt-scoping guarantees. The mitigation text says nothing prompt-derived beyond the keyed lookupTag may be added. The PR also does not show whether the variable is actually forwarded into the LaunchAgent plist (LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys). It sits in the table of forwarded keys, which is documentation only.

This is an unverified contract rather than a finding. The accompanying implementation commits must be reviewed against T-041 (leak #2 closure, per-chunk nonce derivation, TTL, KEK-wipe purge). The table also needs checking for the claim that delta checkpoints preserve cacheSalt scoping and AAD authentication. I flag needs_deeper_review for that reason only. Nothing in this doc diff is itself a security regression.
